description: We are Binary Orbit, a team of two passionate students and Vibe Coders interested in technology and innovation. We have a foundation in frontend development and a basic understanding of backend development. We are currently beginning our journey into Artificial Intelligence, with a particular interest in Machine Learning and Computer Vision. We enjoy learning, experimenting with new technologies, and turning creative ideas into practical solutions.
summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive website that takes visitors through space exploration, from our solar system to the Moon and Mars. Most space content is long text and flat images, which are hard to explore on a phone. This site makes it something visitors can explore, listen to, ask questions about, and test themselves on.

The site has eight sections: a landing page, a Solar System Explorer, Moon and Mars, a 3D artifact museum, a mission timeline, discoveries, a quiz, and a final page.

Key features:

Solar System Explorer: each planet has a name button. Pressing it moves the camera to that planet. Each planet shows a real image and a 3D model. Earth includes the Moon and a satellite, and the Sun includes an orbiting object.
Voice read-out: visitors can hear any text on the site read aloud, which helps people who prefer audio or find reading difficult.
Space chatbot: answers questions about NASA, space, and this project.
Responsive design: works on phones and laptops, with a hamburger menu on mobile.
Quiz and museum: a quiz tests what visitors have learned, and the 3D museum displays space objects.

Tools used: [Framework, e.g. Next.js or React], Tailwind CSS, Three.js for 3D, Vercel for hosting, and [any other tools you used].

Impact: The project makes space science something anyone can explore on any device, with no installation. Audio and the chatbot make the content more accessible, and the quiz and timeline turn browsing into learning.
details:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive web experience that takes visitors through space exploration, from our solar system to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

The site includes a landing page, a Solar System Explorer with 3D planet models (click a planet's name button and the camera focuses on it), an Earth view with the Moon and a satellite, a Sun with an orbiting object, a Moon and Mars section, a 3D artifact museum, a mission timeline, a discoveries section, a quiz, and a final page.

Each planet can show a real image and a 3D model, depending on the device. A voice read-out lets visitors hear the text aloud, which makes the content accessible to people who prefer listening or have reading difficulties. A space chatbot answers questions about NASA, space, and the project.

The site is fully responsive, with a hamburger menu for mobile.

Impact: it turns space science into something people can explore on any phone or laptop, with no installation, and it is designed to be accessible and easy to use.
